title: add nvtx counters, microbench harness, and perf dashboard for runtime
author: Maya Chen
release_notes:
Adds NVTX ranges and counters to the serving runtime, a microbenchmark harness for kernel/scheduling experiments, and a Grafana dashboard with derived counters to track runtime performance regressions. No API changes.

Notes for release: runtime will export NVTX ranges when enabled via REDWOOD_NVTX=1. Microbench is behind a feature flag and not enabled in production builds by default.
description:
Motivation: We need richer, low-overhead runtime instrumentation to diagnose latency outliers and quantify kernel/scheduling optimizations. This PR adds NVTX ranges around key runtime stages, a small set of lightweight atomic counters (per-device kernel exec, memcpy host<->device, batch enqueue/dequeue, kv-cache hits/misses), a microbenchmark harness for continuous-batching and KV cache microbenchmarks, and a Grafana dashboard configuration to visualize the derived metrics.

What this does: 1) NVTX ranges: added scoped NVTX markers around RequestTranslate, BatchEnqueue, KernelLaunch, KVCacheLookup, and ResultSend paths. These are guarded by runtime flag so default performance is unchanged. 2) Counters: lock-free atomics exposed via /metrics endpoint with labels for device_id and model_variant. 3) Microbench harness: new binary tools/microbench/runtime_microbench with workloads: continuous_batching, kv_cache_locality, kernel_latency; supports min/avg/p95 sampling and CSV output. 4) Perf dashboard: grafana/dashboard/runtime_performance.json with panels for per-device token throughput, kernel latency waterfall, KV cache hit-rate, and NVTX range durations.

Checklist: - [x] NVTX ranges added and guarded - [x] Atomic counters and prometheus metrics export - [x] Microbench harness with CI smoke test - [x] Dashboard JSON for internal Grafana - [x] Tests and CI updated - [x] Documentation note in docs/observability/runtime-instrumentation.md

Related: ENG-4521 (profiling roadmap), ENG-4590 (continuous-batching investigation).

review_comments: Diego Rivera requested: guard NVTX with runtime flag and no-op when disabled to avoid overhead in hot paths; also suggested using RNX_TIMING macro to centralize scope entry/exit.
Author (Maya Chen): addressed by adding REDWOOD_NVTX env var and RNX_TIMING wrapper; pushed fix in p3q4r5s commit.
Asha Patel: noted potential false sharing on per-device counters; asked for padding and relaxed atomics. Author updated counter implementation and added unit test.
Liam O'Connor: asked for telemetry naming conventions and recommended adding model_variant label; author confirmed and updated Prometheus exposition.
CI: initial linux-integration job flaked on microbench smoke due to container network race; rerun passed.
Final review: Approvals from Diego and Asha after the p3q4r5s fix; requested squash merge.
merge_details: squash and merge by Maya Chen. Commit message summarized instrumentation, microbench, and dashboard. Merged to main after approvals and green CI.
notes_for_ops: To enable NVTX ranges on a host, set REDWOOD_NVTX=1 and ensure nvtx lib is available on the image. Metrics are exposed at /metrics on the runtime admin port (default 9100). Grafana dashboard JSON can be imported into internal Grafana; it expects prometheus label device_id and model_variant. Microbench should be run on staging GPUs with perf governor set to performance.
